# manju-fenjing-check
**A storyboard quality checker for AI short-form drama, as a DeepSeek Harness plugin.**
Registers one tool, `storyboard_check`. Give it a storyboard segment; it returns a graded report of
everything that will break *before* you pay to render it.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Status: **working, verified end to end against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.2.2-rc.1** — mounted through a `
--patch` overlay, called by the model, report returned intact. The rule engine is deterministic: no
model call, no network, no dependencies.
## The problem
Producing AI short drama means feeding a text-to-video model (Seedance, Kling, Hailuo, Veo) a shot l
ist plus a handful of reference images, one 15-second segment at a time. Five things go wrong over a
nd over, and you usually find out after paying for the render:
| Symptom | Root cause |
| **The face drifts** between shots | Too many character reference images per segment; or a characte
r is told to speak while absent from the frame; or the shot description restates their build and clo

thing, so the model regenerates them |
| **Timing collapses** | Line length does not reconcile with

shot duration; the model averages a 10-shot segment into 3-second chunks |
| **Segments don't connec
t** | The final shot of segment N never states a freeze-frame, so segment N+1 opens on a different w

orld |
| **Platform rejection** | Sensitive-content terms buried in the prompts |
| **Anachronisms**
| A period kitchen stocked with stainless steel and ceramic tile |
This plugin turns those into eight mechanical checks you can run in a second.
## The eight checks
| # | Check | Rule |
| R1 | **Timing ledger** | Dialogue characters ÷ reading rate ≈ seconds, reconciled per shot. Shots

under 2s are flagged; declared totals must match the sum of shot durations. |
| R2 | **Reference bud
get** | Max **2** character reference images per segment. Beyond two, identity weight is split and l

ikeness degrades. Back-only references are useless for a face and get flagged. |
| R3 | **Speaker /
frame mismatch** | A lip-sync directive requires the referenced image to appear in the frame line. O

therwise the model invents a face. Also catches references to images that were never declared. |
| R
4 | **Appearance leakage** | Shot descriptions may state what a character *does*, never what they *l

ook like*. Restating appearance re-rolls the face. |
| R5 | **Prompt hygiene** | Prop and plate imag
es must not depict hands or face fragments (they get welded into the image and contradict the video)
, and must not smuggle in modern objects. Negative-prompt tails are exempt — naming what must not ap

pear is correct usage. |
| R6 | **Freeze-frame chain** | The last shot of a segment must end with an

explicit freeze-frame. Missing it means the next segment starts on a different world. |
| R7 | **Kn
owledge boundary** | Flags wording that hints a character knows more than they could at that moment.

Advisory — semantics need a human. |
| R8 | **Sensitive-term scan** | A 21-term list scanned across
the whole segment. |
Every finding carries a shot number, the offending value, and a concrete fix.

## Try it without installing
A patch overlay mounts the source file directly — good for hacking on the rules:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The plugin path must be absolute; a relative path silently fails to resolve.
## Tool signature
| Parameter | Type | Notes |
| `storyboard` | string, required | The full segment markdown: shot blocks, reference-image prompts,

video-prompt section |
| `chars_per_second` | number | Reading rate for the timing ledger. Default

`4` |
| `max_character_refs` | integer | Reference budget per segment. Default `2` |
Returns `{ blocking, warnings, report }`, where `report` is the rendered text above.
